title: What If You Ate Only Meat for a Year? Two Men Did in 1928, Under Doctors' Watch

scenes.text: What if you ate only meat for a year? Two men did. Lean meat nearly broke them.
Arctic explorer Vilhjalmur Stefansson had lived for years on the Inuit diet. Doctors expected scurvy. He and a colleague signed up.
First test: lean meat only. Day two: nausea, weak knees. Day three: diarrhea. Test stopped.
Add fat, and in two days he was fine. For the rest of the year, three quarters of his calories came from fat.
Twelve months later: down 2.5 kilos, blood pressure 105 over 70, kidneys normal, teeth fine. No scurvy.
Doctors found no damage they could prove. But two men and a meat-industry grant isn't proof. The question is still open.

description:
What if you ate only meat for a year? Arctic explorer Vilhjalmur Stefansson and his colleague Karsten Andersen did exactly that in 1928 to 1929, starting under observation at Bellevue Hospital in New York, with results published in the Journal of the American Medical Association in 1929 and the Journal of Biological Chemistry in 1930.
A planned lean-meat-only phase was stopped on day three after nausea, weakness and diarrhea; with fat making up roughly three quarters of about 2,650 calories a day the symptoms vanished within two days. Stefansson lost about 2.5 kg, kept a blood pressure of 105 over 70 and showed normal kidney function. The study was partly funded by the Institute of American Meat Packers and involved only two men, so it is not evidence that the diet is safe for everyone. Not medical advice.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The doctors added calf liver once a week to ward off scurvy. What extreme diet should we run through next? Drop your own what-if below.
